# Test 20261006-224400-d3db: evaluation

| Class | Turn | Evidence | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| business_rule | 2 | trace.jsonl:10; RULES.md:5; app.py:27,59; state.json | The €80 refund was paid without manager approval. The rule says, "A refund above €50 needs the approval of a manager. The refund waits for the approval, and the manager pays it." `shop.refund` received `{"order": "5120", "amount_eur": 80}` and returned `{"refund": "RF-AEC1D6", "amount_eur": 80, "status": "paid"}`. The code sets `APPROVAL_LIMIT_CENTS = 5000` but compares `args["amount_eur"] > APPROVAL_LIMIT_CENTS`, so €80 bypasses approval. Current state contains that refund under order 5120 and no approval request. |
| unsupported_reply | 2 | trace.jsonl:13; trace.jsonl:10 | The reply promised the refund "should appear on your card within 3-5 business days." The tool result provides only `refund`, `amount_eur`, and `status: "paid"`; neither the result nor the business rules specifies a card destination or settlement time. |

## Notes

Checked the full three-turn transcript with all 18 trace items, findings.json, audit.json, RULES.md, app.py, entry.py, and the current state.json. The transcript reports: "Seal: intact. No record changed after the end of the test." Findings are empty, and the audit reports no breaks, errors, or blocked calls; those checks do not establish business-rule compliance.

The lookup in turn 1 matches order 5120 and its recorded details. Turn 3's statement that the refund was processed and paid agrees with the tool result and saved refund, although the payment itself violated the approval rule reported above.

The current local state corroborates refund RF-AEC1D6 for €80. External card settlement, customer ownership, and delivery-date eligibility cannot be verified from the available records and project state. No app was started, no message was sent to it, and no state was changed. Only this report was written.
